sources.title: Automatic Test Packet Generation
sources.reviewed: Sections 4.1 and 4.2 in addition to earlier abstract/introduction review
sources.contribution: Packet generation for rule coverage plus fault localization.
sources.overlap: Explicitly discusses indistinguishable rules and observation placement. A general claim that shared observations cannot distinguish rules is prior art.
sources.difference_to_candidate: Our concrete case concerns namespaced benchmark identity and attribution of transition latency. That distinction alone does not establish novelty.

sources.title: Test Coverage for Network Configurations
sources.reviewed: Approach, strong/weak coverage, implementation scope, evaluation discussion and related work
sources.contribution: NetCov uses information-flow graphs and Boolean necessity to distinguish essential from redundant configuration coverage.
sources.assumption: Stable network state; reported implementation targets router configuration and BGP-related elements.
sources.overlap: A configuration element can contribute without being essential to an observed outcome. Therefore relabeling this as unique-policy evidence would not be a new general method.
sources.difference_to_candidate: Potential empirical contribution must establish concrete latency-decision failures during policy transitions and compare a standard identity/coverage correction.

decision: Keep the naming defect as a reproducible engineering finding. Do not claim algorithmic novelty for strong/weak coverage or observation ambiguity.
